subject: Hosted API: data residency, retention and deletion questionnaire (EU)
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@acmecorp.com>

Cc: acme-security@acmecorp.com
Date: 2028-09-14T08:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API: data residency and retention questionnaire

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — attaching our standard security questionnaire (ACME_Questionnaire_09282028.xlsx). We're evaluating Redwood for several EU production workloads and need clarification on residency, retention, and deletion practices before we proceed. High-level items we need answered:

- Where is customer content stored for the Hosted API when the customer selects EU? Are all replicas and backups kept inside the EU?
- Default retention for request payloads, logs, and any generated outputs; what options exist to shorten/extend?
- Backup retention windows and how backups are purged (is deletion eventual or immediate across snapshots?).
- Deletion SLA for a full customer erase (live data, replicas, backups) — can you provide a firm timeline and proof of deletion?
- Do you ever use customer content to train or fine-tune models? If not, how is that guaranteed operationally?
- Key management: do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for Hosted API customers in the EU?

We'd appreciate a written response we can share internally (Security & Legal). Target: responses by EOD Friday (2028-09-15). If this needs more time, please advise ETA.

Thanks,
Elena Gomez
Senior Information Security Manager
AcmeCorp

Attachment: ACME_Questionnaire_09282028.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>

Date: 2028-09-14T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API: data residency and retention questionnaire

Elena —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the clear list. Quick summary up front, and Irene/kimberly are looped in for the detailed follow-up and evidence pack.

Top-line (short answers)
- Residency: For customers who select the EU region, primary data, replicas, and routine backups are geo-fenced to EU regions (we operate across multiple EU zones).
- Default retention: ephemeral request cache (14 days); request logs and short-term diagnostics (30 days by default). Longer retention is available via addendum.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots retained for 90 days by default; deletion of snapshots is processed via background jobs and completes across live replicas and backup stores (see detailed below).
- Deletion SLA: standard Hosted API customers: 30 days end-to-end purge; Enterprise addendum can shorten to a contractual 7–14 day SLA.
- Model training: Redwood does not use customer request content to train public models. We segregate telemetry used for product metrics; customer data is never mixed into model training corpora.
- KMS: Hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed keys (CMKs) are available for EU enterprise customers as part of the Private/enterprise add-on.

I've attached a short PDF (hostedapi-residency-answers-jonas.pdf) with the summary and pointers — Irene will provide the technical deletion/playbook and retention matrix requested.

If you need a firm contractual commitment (7-day erase), we can prepare an addendum and a DocuSign route — happy to set that up once you've reviewed the details.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachment: hostedapi-residency-answers-jonas.pdf (application/pdf)

4) Training guarantee: is there a signed policy or SOC2 control that we can reference that shows request content is excluded from model training pipelines?

Also please confirm whether log exports (audit logs, access logs) can be provided on-demand for a rolling 365-day window in CSV/JSON.

We are trying to avoid a long procurement cycle, but the deletion SLA requirement is critical for Data Protection Assessment — can Redwood commit to 7 days for EEA customers if we sign the addendum?

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Below are the technical clarifications and the operational evidence we can provide. I've attached a concise Data Deletion Playbook and a retention matrix CSV for account-level options.

1) Geo-fencing and DR
- For customers who select the EU residency option, all primary live stores and automated replica sets are constrained to our EU region pool (AWS eu-west-1, eu-central-1 equivalents).
- Backups: routine (scheduled) encrypted snapshots are retained in the same EU region pool.
- DR / failover: we do have the ability to fail over between EU regions only — we do not replicate EU-resident customer data to non-EU regions for normal DR. Cross-continent replication only occurs with explicit customer consent or if the customer contracts a global DR footprint (this is not enabled by default).

2) Backup retention and purge behavior
- Default scheduled snapshot retention: 90 days rolling. Snapshots are tagged with account id and retention expiry.
- Deletion workflow: when a deletion request is initiated, it triggers (a) removal from live stores, (b) background jobs that mark associated snapshots for expedited purge, and (c) queueing of deletion tasks to remove cached copies across CDN/edge caches.
- Snapshot purge is executed in parallel with background compaction jobs; full removal from all backup layers is eventually consistent and completes per the SLA negotiated (standard: 30 days; accelerated: 7 days for addendum).

3) Evidence and audit trail
- We provide a machine-readable deletion record that includes: job ID, initiating principal, timestamp (UTC), affected storage IDs, and final status. We can export the record as JSON and include S3 object keys or snapshot IDs where applicable.
- Audit logs: we can provision export access to audit/access logs for a rolling 365-day window in JSON/CSV; exports are delivered via a secure presigned link or shared S3 bucket depending on preference.

4) Retention configuration
- By default, the 14/30/90 schedule is our hosted baseline. Account-level modification of those values requires either an Enterprise setting in the Console (for some values) or a contractual addendum for guaranteed immutable retention windows. The retention-matrix.csv lists the options by tier.

5) Model training and data usage
- Operational guarantee: customer request/response payloads are excluded from model training pipelines. We enforce this through data tagging and an internal isolation policy; telemetry used for product metric aggregation is anonymized and aggregated.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and internal policy excerpts can be provided. If you need an explicit contractual clause prohibiting training use, we can add that to the addendum.

6) Key management
- Hosted default: Redwood-managed keys (KMS).
- CMK option: for EU enterprise customers we offer a customer-managed key integration (AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault) as a paid enterprise option; keys remain under your control, and Redwood never exports key material.

Attachments included with this message: data-deletion-playbook.pdf, retention-matrix.csv.

If you confirm that a 7-day deletion SLA is required for your EEA tenants, we will prepare an addendum and a DocuSign route (that addendum will include the accelerated purge procedure and scheduling for test erasure).

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through any of the above.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
